quotes.english: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

articles.title: Why China loves watching the 世界杯 (World Cup)
articles.body:
大家好，欢迎回到 MaoMi Chinese！

最近，世界上很多人都在看足球世界杯。说到足球，你可能会想到巴西、阿根廷、英国、德国。但是，你会想到中国吗？ 很多人会问：中国有这么多人，为什么足球踢得不好？中国人喜欢足球吗？中国人怎么看自己的国家队？今天，我们一起来聊一聊中国的足球吧！

其实，中国人很喜欢足球。在中国，足球是最受欢迎的运动之一。很多人从小就踢足球。每到世界杯，很多中国球迷都会熬夜。球迷，意思是喜欢看足球比赛的人。熬夜，意思是很晚睡觉，或者不睡觉
articles.body_en: Hi everyone, welcome back to MaoMi Chinese! Lately a lot of people around the world have been watching the football World Cup. When football comes up you might think of Brazil, Argentina, England or Germany — but would you think of China? Many people ask: China has so many people, so why is its football not better? And what do Chinese people make of it?

articles.title: How to use 为了 (wei le)?
articles.body: 为了 表示目的。我们用它来说明做某件事的原因和目标。这是一个很常用的语法结构，在书面语和口语中都很常见。
articles.body_en: "为了" expresses purpose. We use it to explain the reason and goal behind doing something. It is a very common grammatical structure, appearing frequently in both written and spoken Chinese.

articles.title: The Story of 中秋节
articles.body: 中秋节是中国重要的传统节日。每年农历八月十五，家人团聚，一起吃月饼、赏月，寄托对家人的思念。
articles.body_en: The Mid-Autumn Festival is one of China's most important traditional holidays. On the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month families come together to eat mooncakes and look at the moon, carrying their feelings for the people they miss.

articles.title: Take good care of yourself — 好好照顾自己
articles.body: 我觉得也是，专注爱自己，好好喂养自己，吃健康的食物，做爱做的事，通过学习知识提升自己，无论是业务还是身体，不需要在乎别人！
articles.body_en: I think so too — focus on loving yourself, feed yourself well, eat healthy food, do what you love, and lift yourself up by learning. Whether it is your work or your body, you do not need to worry about what anyone else thinks.

articles.title: Xiao Ming's first day — 小明的第一天
articles.body:
今天是小明的第一天。他很早就起床了。

他说：“你好，我叫小明。”老师说：“欢迎你！”

同学们都很好。中午他们一起吃饭。小明很高兴。

下午三点，他回家了。他想：明天我还要来。
articles.body_en:
Today is Xiao Ming's first day. He got up very early.

He said, "Hello, my name is Xiao Ming." The teacher said, "Welcome!"

His classmates were all kind. At noon they ate together. Xiao Ming was very happy.

At three in the afternoon he went home. He thought: tomorrow I want to come again.

articles.title: A bowl of noodles — 一碗面
articles.body:
下雨了。小美没有带伞，衣服都湿了。

她走进一家很小的面馆。老板说：“坐吧，先喝点热水。”

面来了，很香。小美吃得很慢，因为外面还在下雨，她不想走。

走的时候，老板给了她一把旧伞。“下次还我就好。”

那把伞，小美用了三年。
articles.body_en:
It started to rain. Xiao Mei had no umbrella and her clothes were soaked.

She stepped into a very small noodle shop. The owner said, "Sit down, have some hot water first."

The noodles came, and they smelled wonderful. Xiao Mei ate slowly, because it was still raining outside and she did not want to leave.

As she left, the owner handed her an old umbrella. "Just return it next time."

Xiao Mei used that umbrella for three years.

articles.title: Ten minutes in a 出租车 (taxi)
articles.body:
“师傅，去机场，谢谢。”

司机看了看表：“现在有点堵，可能要四十分钟。”

我有点着急，一直看手机。司机说：“别急，你的飞机几点？”

“晚上八点。”

他笑了：“那还早。年轻人，路上也是时间啊。”

后来我们聊了十分钟。到机场的时候，我发现自己一点也不急了。
articles.body_en:
"Driver, to the airport, thank you."

He glanced at the clock. "Traffic is bad right now — it might take forty minutes."

I was anxious and kept checking my phone. The driver said, "Don't rush. What time is your flight?"

"Eight in the evening."

He smiled. "Then there's plenty of time. Young man, the journey is time too."

We talked for ten minutes after that. By the time we reached the airport, I found I wasn't in a hurry at all.

articles.title: How Chinese people say 谢谢 (thank you)
articles.body:
在中国，越亲近的人，说“谢谢”越少。

对服务员、同事、陌生人，我们常说“谢谢”。但是在家里，帮妈妈拿东西，她可能只说“好”。

这不是没有礼貌。太客气反而让人觉得有距离。

所以听到朋友说“跟我还客气什么”，那是好事——他把你当自己人。
articles.body_en:
In China, the closer you are to someone, the less you say "thank you".

With waiters, colleagues and strangers we say 谢谢 often. But at home, if you pass your mother something, she might just say "good".

This is not rudeness. Being too polite can actually feel like distance.

So if a friend says "why so formal with me?", that is a good sign — they consider you one of their own.

articles.title: Why you can't say 一个茶 — measure words
articles.body:
中文里，数字和名词中间要有量词。

所以不说“一个茶”，说“一杯茶”。不说“三个面包”，一般说“三片面包”。

量词常常和东西的样子有关：平的用“张”（一张纸），长的用“条”（一条鱼），本子用“本”（一本书）。

不知道用哪个的时候，先用“个”。别人听得懂，慢慢就记住了。
articles.body_en:
In Chinese, a measure word sits between the number and the noun.

So you don't say 一个茶, you say 一杯茶 (a cup of tea). Not 三个面包 but usually 三片面包 (three slices of bread).

Measure words often relate to an object's shape: flat things take 张 (一张纸, a sheet of paper), long things take 条 (一条鱼, a fish), and bound things take 本 (一本书, a book).

When you don't know which to use, start with 个. People will understand you, and the rest comes with time.

articles.title: Lucky 八, unlucky 四
articles.body:
在中国，“八”是很受欢迎的数字，因为它听起来像“发”，有发财的意思。

“四”听起来像“死”，所以很多楼没有四层，电话号码里也常常没有四。

下次看电梯的时候，可以找一找：有没有 4 楼？
articles.body_en:
In China 八 (eight) is a well-liked number, because it sounds like 发 — to prosper.

四 (four) sounds like 死 (death), so many buildings have no fourth floor, and phone numbers often avoid it.

Next time you're in a lift, have a look: is there a floor 4?

articles.title: Three 老歌 (old songs) everyone in China can sing
articles.body:
在中国，有几首歌几乎人人都会唱。

第一首是《月亮代表我的心》。歌词很简单，很多外国人学中文的时候都听过。

第二首是《朋友》。同学毕业的时候常常一起唱。

第三首是《海阔天空》。这是广东话的歌，可是全中国都在听。

听歌学中文很好，因为歌词慢，也会重复。
articles.body_en:
In China there are a few songs almost everyone can sing.

The first is "The Moon Represents My Heart". The lyrics are simple, and many foreigners hear it while learning Chinese.

The second is "Friends", often sung together by classmates at graduation.

The third is "Boundless Sea and Sky". It is a Cantonese song, but the whole country listens to it.

Learning Chinese through songs works well, because lyrics are slow and they repeat.

articles.title: Why Chinese films happen at the 饭桌 (dinner table)
articles.body:
看中国电影的时候，你会发现很多重要的事情都发生在饭桌上。

谈生意在饭桌上，见家长在饭桌上，吵架也在饭桌上。

这不是导演偷懒。在中国文化里，一起吃饭代表关系近。

所以下次看中国电影，可以看看谁坐在中间，谁先动筷子——里面有很多信息。
articles.body_en:
Watch Chinese films and you notice how much of the important business happens at a dining table.

Deals are done at the table, families meet at the table, arguments break out at the table.

This is not the director being lazy. In Chinese culture, eating together means the relationship is close.

So next time, watch who sits in the middle and who picks up their chopsticks first — there is a lot of information in it.

articles.title: Where the 高铁 (high-speed rail) can take you
articles.body:
在中国旅行，高铁常常比飞机方便。

车站在市中心，不用提前两个小时到，票也可以用手机买。

北京到上海大概五个小时。西安到成都三个小时。

上车以后可以看看窗外——从北方到南方，房子和田地都会慢慢变样子。
articles.body_en:
Travelling in China, the high-speed train is often easier than flying.

Stations are in the city centre, you do not need to arrive two hours early, and tickets are bought on your phone.

Beijing to Shanghai is about five hours. Xi'an to Chengdu is three.

Once you are on board, look out of the window — as you go from north to south, the houses and the fields slowly change shape.

articles.title: Three sentences for 问路 (asking directions)
articles.body:
在中国问路，其实三句话就够了。

第一句：“请问，地铁站在哪儿？”

第二句：“走路要多长时间？”

第三句：“谢谢！”

如果没听懂，可以说“请再说一遍，慢一点”。大家都会很有耐心。
articles.body_en:
Asking for directions in China really only takes three sentences.

First: "Excuse me, where is the subway station?"

Second: "How long does it take to walk?"

Third: "Thank you!"

If you did not catch the answer, say "please say it again, a bit slower". People are patient about it.

articles.title: What to say in your first meeting — 第一次开会说什么
articles.body:
在中国公司开会，开始的时候常常先说一句：“大家好，我先简单说一下。”

有意见的时候，很少直接说“我不同意”。多数人会说“我有一个小小的想法”或者“我们要不要再看看？”

这不是不诚实，是给对方留面子。

听懂这些说法，比背很多商务词更有用。
articles.body_en:
In a Chinese company meeting, people often open with "Hello everyone, let me say a few words first."

When someone disagrees, they rarely say "I disagree" outright. Most will say "I have a small thought" or "shall we take another look at this?"

This is not dishonesty. It leaves the other person their face.

Understanding these phrasings is more useful than memorising a pile of business vocabulary.

articles.title: How to read a Chinese 名片 (business card)
articles.body:
收到名片的时候，要用两只手接，然后看一看再放好。马上放进口袋是不礼貌的。

名片上常见的字有：经理、总监、助理、部门。

“王经理”这样叫人很常见——姓在前，职位在后。叫“王先生”也可以，可是在公司里，职位听起来更客气。
articles.body_en:
When you are handed a business card, take it with both hands, look at it, then put it away. Pocketing it straight away is impolite.

Common words on a card: manager, director, assistant, department.

Addressing someone as "Manager Wang" is very normal — surname first, title after. "Mr Wang" is fine too, but inside a company the title sounds more respectful.

articles.title: How to open and close a Chinese 邮件 (email)
articles.body:
中文邮件的开头很短：“您好，”就够了。

结尾常常写“谢谢”或者“祝好”，然后写自己的名字。

中间不用写很长的客气话。中文的商务邮件比英文短，说清楚事情最重要。
articles.body_en:
The opening of a Chinese email is short: "Hello," is enough.

The ending is usually "thank you" or "best wishes", followed by your name.

There is no need for long courtesies in between. Chinese business email is shorter than English — saying the thing clearly is what matters.

podcasts.title: Will Our Digital Clone Replace Us? 数字人会取代我们吗？
podcasts.transcript:
大家好，欢迎回来
最近，在中国的社交媒体上，很多人都在讨论数字人。什么是数字人呢？简单说，就是用 AI 做出来的“人”。数字人不是真的人，是AI，但是可以像人一样工作，回答问题，解决问题。这是一个好事，还是一个可怕的事呢？今天，我们一起来聊一聊吧！

在中国，很多工作已经开始用数字人了。有AI演员，很多短视频都是AI做的，演员都是AI演员。很多广告里的人不是真的人，而是AI。有 AI 主播，有的电视台已经用数字人来报新闻了，他们可以一天工作 24 小时，不会累，也不会请假。还有一些公司，会把员工平时开会的录音、写的邮件、工作的习惯，都整理起来，做成一个“数字分身”。这样就算员工不在这里工作了，这个“数字人”也可以继续帮公司回答问题，做简单的工作。

社交媒体上，很多网友开始讨论了。有的人觉得很方便，有人说：“太好了，以后半夜也可以有人帮我解决问题。”还有做老板的人觉得，这样可以省很多钱，不用一直找新员工。但是，更多人觉得很可怕。有网友觉得，如果他们不在公司工作了，公司还用他们的数字人来工作，那这个还是他们吗？也有网友问：“公司用我的声音、我的脸，这合法的吗？”合法，也就是在法律上是对的。

最近在中国，有一家视频公司的老板说，他们以后要用AI演员，大家听了以后都很生气。大家都说，只要你们敢用AI演员，我们就再也不看你们的电视剧！一方面，大家觉得，AI电视剧没有“人味”，觉得AI做的东西没什么感情。另一方面，大家都很担心，如果越来越多工作可以被数字人代替，那真的人怎么办？是不是会有很多人失业？但是也有人觉得还好，他们觉得需要有人来做AI，所以会有新的工作。

如果有一天，你的公司想用你的数据做一个数字人，你会同意吗？欢迎给我们留言，分享你的看法！
podcasts.bio: AI actors, AI news presenters, even your "digital clone" still working after you leave... Digital humans are changing everything. Convenient or creepy? Let's explore what's really happening in China, and what it means for you.

podcasts.title: 在咖啡店点单 - Ordering at the Coffee Shop
podcasts.transcript:
服务员：您好，请问喝点什么？
李明：我要一杯热拿铁，中杯。
服务员：好的。还需要别的吗？
李明：再来一块蛋糕吧。
服务员：一共三十八块。
李明：可以用手机付吗？

李明：好，扫好了。
服务员：请稍等，好了我叫您。

Server: Hello, what would you like to drink?
Li Ming: I'll have a hot latte, medium.
Server: All right. Anything else?
Li Ming: A slice of cake as well.
Server: That's thirty-eight yuan altogether.
Li Ming: Can I pay by phone?
Server: Yes, just scan this code.
Li Ming: Done.
Server: One moment please, I'll call you when it's ready.

podcasts.title: 问路 - Asking for Directions
podcasts.transcript:
安娜：请问，地铁站在哪儿？
路人：一直走，到红绿灯往左拐。
安娜：远吗？
路人：不远，走五分钟就到了。
安娜：那附近有银行吗？
路人：有，就在地铁站旁边。
安娜：太好了，谢谢您！
路人：不客气。
podcasts.bio: How to ask where something is, and how to understand the answer you get back. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Anna: Excuse me, where is the subway station?
Passer-by: Go straight, then turn left at the traffic lights.
Anna: Is it far?
Passer-by: Not far, about five minutes on foot.
Anna: Is there a bank near there?
Passer-by: Yes, right next to the station.
Anna: Wonderful, thank you!
Passer-by: You're welcome.

podcasts.title: 坐高铁去上海 - Taking the High-Speed Train to Shanghai
podcasts.transcript:
王朋：我想买一张去上海的高铁票。
售票员：什么时候的？
王朋：明天上午，越早越好。
售票员：八点十分有一班，二等座五百五。
王朋：要多久？
售票员：四个半小时。
王朋：就这班吧。请问在哪个站台？
售票员：票上会写，一般提前二十分钟检票。
王朋：明白了，谢谢。
podcasts.bio: Buying a ticket, finding the platform, and what the announcements actually say. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Wang Peng: I'd like a high-speed train ticket to Shanghai.
Clerk: For when?
Wang Peng: Tomorrow morning, as early as possible.
Clerk: There's one at 8:10, second class is 550.
Wang Peng: How long does it take?
Clerk: Four and a half hours.
Wang Peng: I'll take that one. Which platform?
Clerk: It's printed on the ticket — boarding usually opens twenty minutes ahead.
Wang Peng: Understood, thank you.

podcasts.title: 在酒店办入住 - Checking Into a Hotel
podcasts.transcript:
前台：您好，请出示一下护照。
安娜：给您。我订了一间大床房。
前台：找到了，住三晚，对吗？
安娜：对。请问早餐几点开始？
前台：六点半到十点，在二楼。
安娜：房间的网络怎么连？
前台：房卡背面有密码。
安娜：好的。对了，能换一间安静一点的吗？
前台：可以，我给您换到高层。
podcasts.bio: Checking in, asking about breakfast, and sorting out a problem with the room. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Reception: Hello, may I see your passport?
Anna: Here you are. I booked a room with a double bed.
Reception: Found it — three nights, is that right?
Anna: Yes. What time does breakfast start?
Reception: Six thirty to ten, on the second floor.
Anna: How do I connect to the room's wifi?
Reception: The password is on the back of your key card.
Anna: Right. Actually, could I have a quieter room?
Reception: Of course, I'll move you to a higher floor.

podcasts.title: 第一次开会 - Your First Meeting
podcasts.transcript:
张经理：今天我们讨论下个月的计划。
李明：好的，我先说说市场部分。
张经理：请讲。
李明：我们打算先做一个小范围的测试。
张经理：需要多长时间？
李明：大概两个星期。
张经理：预算呢？
李明：这部分我还在算，明天给您一个数字，可以吗？
张经理：可以。那就先这样。
podcasts.bio: Introducing yourself, following an agenda, and saying you need more time. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Manager Zhang: Today we're discussing next month's plan.
Li Ming: All right, I'll start with the marketing side.
Manager Zhang: Go ahead.
Li Ming: We intend to run a small-scale test first.
Manager Zhang: How long will it take?
Li Ming: About two weeks.
Manager Zhang: And the budget?
Li Ming: I'm still working that out — could I give you a figure tomorrow?
Manager Zhang: That's fine. Let's leave it there for now.

podcasts.title: 谈价格 - Negotiating a Price
podcasts.transcript:
供应商：这个价格已经很低了。
采购：我理解，可是我们的量也不小。
供应商：您希望多少？
采购：如果一次订两千件，能不能再降百分之五？
供应商：百分之五有点难，百分之三我可以做主。
采购：那付款方式上能灵活一点吗？
供应商：可以，先付三成，剩下的发货后一个月。
采购：这样我可以接受。
供应商：那我下午把合同发给您。
podcasts.bio: How a price conversation is actually conducted — softening, conceding, and closing. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Supplier: This price is already very low.
Buyer: I understand, but our volume isn't small either.
Supplier: What figure did you have in mind?
Buyer: If we order two thousand units at once, could you come down another five percent?
Supplier: Five is difficult; three I can authorise myself.
Buyer: Then could you be flexible on payment terms?
Supplier: Yes — thirty percent up front, the rest a month after delivery.
Buyer: I can accept that.
Supplier: I'll send the contract over this afternoon.

podcasts.title: 春节回家 - Going Home for Spring Festival
podcasts.transcript:
小明：你今年回家过年吗？
安娜：回，票已经买好了。
小明：抢到票不容易吧？
安娜：真的很难，我提前一个月就开始刷。
小明：除夕晚上你们家做什么？
安娜：一家人一起包饺子，看春晚。
小明：有红包吗？
安娜：小孩子有，我早就过了那个年纪了。
小明：哈哈，我也是。
podcasts.bio: Why the whole country moves at once, and what actually happens on the night. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Xiao Ming: Are you going home for New Year this year?
Anna: Yes, I've already bought my ticket.
Xiao Ming: Getting one can't have been easy.
Anna: It was really hard — I started refreshing a month in advance.
Xiao Ming: What does your family do on New Year's Eve?
Anna: We make dumplings together and watch the gala.
Xiao Ming: Any red envelopes?
Anna: For the children. I'm long past that age.
Xiao Ming: Ha, so am I.

podcasts.title: 中国人的送礼 - Giving Gifts in China
podcasts.transcript:
安娜：去朋友家吃饭，我应该带什么？
小明：水果就很好，或者一盒茶。
安娜：送钟可以吗？
小明：千万不要，送钟听起来不吉利。
安娜：为什么？
小明：因为跟“送终”一个音。
安娜：原来是这样。那梨呢？

podcasts.bio: What to bring, what to avoid, and why the gift is refused twice before it is taken. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Anna: If I'm going to a friend's house for dinner, what should I bring?
Xiao Ming: Fruit is fine, or a box of tea.
Anna: Would a clock be all right?

Anna: Why is that?

podcasts.title: 手机支付改变了什么 - What Mobile Payment Changed
podcasts.transcript:
主持人：现在出门你还带现金吗？
嘉宾：几乎不带了，一个手机就够了。
主持人：什么时候开始的？
嘉宾：大概十年前，从买菜开始，慢慢地连路边摊都能扫码。
主持人：这样方便，但也有问题吧？
嘉宾：有。老年人不太会用，有些人没有智能手机。
主持人：后来怎么解决的？
嘉宾：现在很多地方规定必须收现金，不能拒收。
主持人：技术跑得快，规则也得跟上。
podcasts.bio: How cash disappeared from daily life, and what that means for people it left behind. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Host: Do you still carry cash when you go out?
Guest: Almost never — a phone is enough.
Host: When did that start?
Guest: About ten years ago, beginning with groceries, and gradually even street stalls took QR codes.
Host: Convenient, but surely there are problems?
Guest: There are. Older people find it hard to use, and some don't have smartphones.
Host: How was that addressed?
Guest: Many places are now required to accept cash and cannot refuse it.
Host: Technology moves fast, and the rules have to keep up.

podcasts.title: 大城市还是小城市 - Big City or Small City
podcasts.transcript:
小明：你毕业以后打算留在北京吗？

小明：我有个朋友回老家了，说过得轻松多了。
安娜：轻松是轻松，可是选择也少。
小明：现在有些中等城市发展得很快。
安娜：对，我也在看那边的岗位。
小明：所以关键不是大和小，是你想要什么样的生活。
安娜：说得对。
podcasts.bio: The trade-off a generation is arguing about: opportunity against the cost of staying. Written for Verbo. Recording to follow.
podcasts.transcript_en:
Xiao Ming: Are you planning to stay in Beijing after you graduate?
Anna: I haven't decided. There are more jobs, but the rent is too high.
Xiao Ming: A friend of mine went back to his hometown and says life is much easier.
Anna: Easier, yes, but there's less choice too.
Xiao Ming: Some mid-sized cities are growing quickly now.
Anna: True — I'm looking at positions there as well.
Xiao Ming: So the question isn't big or small, it's what kind of life you want.
Anna: That's right.

study_units.title: 他在哪儿呢？ - Where is he?
study_units.description: Ask where someone is and say where things are.
study_units.culture_body: University libraries in China fill up early, especially before exams. Students often arrive at opening time to claim a seat, and it is common to see a book or a water bottle left on a desk to hold a place for the rest of the day.

study_units.title: 这是我朋友送给我的 - This was a gift from my friend
study_units.description: Talk about presents and say who gave you something.
study_units.culture_body: Gift choice carries meaning in China. Clocks are avoided because 送钟 (sòng zhōng) sounds like attending a funeral, and pears are shared with care because 梨 (lí) sounds like 离, to part. Red packaging, on the other hand, is always welcome.

study_units.title: 上午九点上课 - Class starts at nine in the morning
study_units.description: Give times of day and say when things happen.
study_units.culture_body: Many schools and offices in China pause for 午休 (wǔxiū), a rest after lunch that can run from noon to two. Students often nap at their desks, and the working day simply extends later into the evening to make up for it.

study_units.title: 我可以坐这儿吗？ - May I sit here?
study_units.description: Ask permission politely and answer someone who asks you.
study_units.culture_body: In busy Chinese restaurants, strangers often share a table — 拼桌 (pīnzhuō). Asking 我可以坐这儿吗？ before sitting down is the normal courtesy, and a nod in reply is answer enough.

study_units.title: 我每天六点起床 - I get up at six every day
study_units.description: Describe a daily routine in order.
study_units.culture_body: Parks across China fill soon after dawn with 晨练 (chénliàn) — morning exercise. Groups practise tai chi, dance, or badminton together, and it is mostly older people who keep the tradition going, often meeting the same friends daily for years.

study_units.title: 你的爱好是什么？ - What is your hobby?
study_units.description: Say what you like doing and ask others about their interests.
study_units.culture_body: In the evening, public squares across China host 广场舞 (guǎngchǎngwǔ) — square dancing. Groups of mostly middle-aged and older women dance together to music, and it has become one of the most visible forms of social exercise in the country.

study_units.title: 你怎么了？ - What is wrong?
study_units.description: Say you are unwell and take advice about it.
study_units.culture_body: The stock piece of advice for almost any ailment in China is 多喝热水 (duō hē rè shuǐ) — "drink more hot water". Cold drinks are widely believed to be hard on the body, and restaurants often serve warm water by default.

study_grammar_points.title: Serial Verb Sentences (2)
study_grammar_points.description: Serial verb sentences featuring the particle 着 describe a secondary action that indicates the state, manner, or background under which the main action occurs.

study_grammar_points.title: 几点 — asking what time
study_grammar_points.description: 几 asks for a number and 点 means o’clock, so 几点 asks "what time". It goes where the time would go in the answer, not at the end of the sentence.

study_grammar_points.title: 在 — saying where something is
study_grammar_points.description: 在 is a verb on its own, not a preposition here. It needs no other verb after it: 我在图书馆 is a complete sentence meaning "I am at the library".

study_grammar_points.title: 呢 — asking the same question back
study_grammar_points.description: Putting 呢 after a noun repeats the question you were just asked, without saying it again. "我很好，你呢？" means "I am well, and you?"

study_grammar_points.title: 是…的 — highlighting how or by whom
study_grammar_points.description: When something has already happened and you want to point at who did it, or when or how, put that part between 是 and 的. The listener already knows the event; 是…的 says which detail matters.
study_grammar_points.structure: 是 + (who / when / how) + Verb + 的

study_grammar_points.title: 送给 — giving to someone
study_grammar_points.description: 给 marks who receives the thing. It follows the verb directly, and the receiver comes straight after it.

study_grammar_points.title: Time words come BEFORE the verb
study_grammar_points.description: This is the opposite of English. The time is part of the setting, so Chinese states it first and then says what happened. "I get up at seven" is literally "I at-seven get up".

study_grammar_points.title: Telling the time: 点, 分, 半
study_grammar_points.description: 点 is the hour, 分 the minute, and 半 stands in for thirty. 两点 is used for two o'clock, not 二点.

study_grammar_points.title: 可以 — asking for permission
study_grammar_points.description: 可以 asks whether something is allowed, where 会 asks whether you know how and 能 asks whether it is physically possible. Adding 吗 turns it into a question.

study_grammar_points.title: 请问 — opening a question to a stranger
study_grammar_points.description: 请问 goes at the very front of the sentence, before the question itself. It is what makes the question polite rather than abrupt.

study_grammar_points.title: 以后 — after doing something
study_grammar_points.description: Unlike English "after", 以后 comes at the END of the clause it applies to. "After I get up" is 起床以后, literally "get-up after".

study_grammar_points.title: 然后 — and then
study_grammar_points.description: 然后 links the next thing in a sequence and starts its own clause. It describes order, not cause.

study_grammar_points.title: 喜欢 + verb — saying what you like doing
study_grammar_points.description: 喜欢 can be followed straight by another verb, with nothing in between. There is no equivalent of the English "to" or "-ing".

study_grammar_points.title: 吧 — making a suggestion
study_grammar_points.description: Ending a sentence with 吧 softens it from an instruction into a suggestion the other person can decline.

study_grammar_points.title: 怎么了 — asking what has happened
study_grammar_points.description: 怎么了 asks what has gone wrong, and the 了 is what makes it about a change — something is different from before. It stands as a whole question on its own.

study_grammar_points.title: 还没有 — not yet
study_grammar_points.description: 还没有 says an action has not happened SO FAR, leaving it open. 不 would refuse it outright; 还没有 simply means it is still to come.
